deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is a draft of the theta-vanishing argument of Riemann's 'Ueber das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen' (Crelle 65, 1866). The notation follows 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857).
- The u_π (π=1..p) are normalized integrals of the first kind on the surface T of genus p.
- α_π^{(ν)} denotes u_π(η_ν), the value at the point η_ν.
- ϑ(v) = Σ_m exp(Σ a_{ππ'} m_π m_π' + 2 Σ m_π v_π).
- The additive constants of the u are assumed chosen so that the following holds (assumption carried over from earlier pages, which are not available): for generic e, ϑ(u − e) as a function on T has exactly p zeros η_1..η_p, and Σ_1^p α^{(ν)} ≡ e modulo periods.

Step 1 (sufficiency). If v ≡ −Σ_{ν=1}^{p−1} α^{(ν)} for some p−1 points, then ϑ(v) = 0. The first lines restate this conclusion of the earlier argument. Proof [mine, standard]: put e = α^{(p)} − v. Then e ≡ Σ_1^p α^{(ν)}, so ϑ(u − e) vanishes at η_p, i.e. at u = α^{(p)}, giving ϑ(v) = 0.

Step 2 (necessity). Suppose ϑ(v) = 0.
- Choose η_p arbitrarily and consider ϑ(u − α^{(p)} + v) on T, i.e. take e = α^{(p)} − v. (The transcribed line 'v_p = u_p − α_p^p + v_p' should read this way.)
- This function vanishes at η_p, because at that point its argument is v.
- By the zero theorem it vanishes to first order at p−1 further points η_1..η_{p−1}.
- Then (α^{(p)} − v) ≡ Σ_1^p α^{(ν)}, hence v ≡ −Σ_1^{p−1} α^{(ν)}.
- Conclusion: the zero set of ϑ is exactly {−Σ_1^{p−1} α(η_ν)}.

Step 3 (evenness). Replacing m by −m in the series leaves its value unchanged, so ϑ(−v) = ϑ(v).

Step 4.
- Take η_1..η_{p−1} arbitrary. By Step 1, ϑ(−Σ_1^{p−1}α) = 0, so by evenness ϑ(Σ_1^{p−1}α) = 0.
- By Step 2 there are p−1 points η_p..η_{2p−2} with Σ_1^{p−1} α ≡ −Σ_p^{2p−2} α.
- Hence (Σ_1^{2p−2} α_1^{(ν)}, ..., Σ_1^{2p−2} α_p^{(ν)}) ≡ (0, ..., 0).

Step 5.
- The last p−1 points depend on the first p−1 so that Σ_1^{2p−2} dα_π^{(ν)} = 0 for π = 1..p.
- By the inversion of Abel's theorem (treated on the next page), the 2p−2 points are the zeros of a differential of the first kind. Equivalently, they are the points where an integral of the first kind becomes infinitely small of the second order (i.e. its differential vanishes).
- Writing (σ_ν, ζ_ν) for the values of (s, z) at η_ν, these are the common roots of F(s,z) = 0 and c_1φ^{(1)} + ... + c_pφ^{(p)} = 0 with arbitrary c. The fixed common roots at the singular points of F are excluded.
- Thus, with this normalization, the image of the canonical divisor under the Abel map is ≡ 0. In modern terms: the theta divisor is W_{p−1} − κ, and 2κ ≡ image of K, absorbed into the choice of constants.
errors: Step 2 needs ϑ(u − α(η_p) + v) not to vanish identically on T. This fails for every choice of η_p when v lies in the singular locus of the theta divisor (v ↔ D with h^0(D) ≥ 2, by Riemann's singularity theorem). So 'η_p beliebig wählt' is not justified there. A limit/closure argument is needed, which Riemann supplies in the published 1866 paper; it is not on this page.

Step 5's claim that the 2p−2 points form the zero set of a φ uses the converse of Abel's theorem plus genericity of η_1..η_{p−1}. Genericity ensures the residual p−1 points are uniquely determined. This is asserted, not proved, here.
The normalization of the additive constants (vanishing of the vector of Riemann constants up to the stated convention) is implicit; it is not stated on this page.
The upper index 'p−2' in Σ_1^{p−2} α_p^{(ν)} is a slip (of the transcription or the hand); it should be p−1.

results.what: ϑ(v)=0 iff v ≡ −Σ_{ν=1}^{p−1} u(η_ν) for some p−1 points (with suitably normalized constants)
ϑ(−v)=ϑ(v) via m→−m in the series
results.modern_name: evenness of the Riemann theta function

results.what: With this normalization, the Abel image of the 2p−2 zeros of any differential of the first kind is ≡ 0; the residual points of a generic (p−1)-tuple are the rest of a canonical divisor
results.modern_name: 2κ ≡ canonical class / Riemann constant and canonical divisor

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the published 1866 paper 'Ueber das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen'. Its results (the vanishing theorem, evenness, and the canonical-divisor relation) are well known as Riemann's.

checkable.asserts: Symmetric truncation of the genus-1 theta series is even in v (the m→−m argument). Expected result: 0.
The p−1 arbitrary points plus the p−1 determined points total 2p−2, the degree of a canonical divisor. Expected result: 0.
Hyperelliptic y^2=f(x), deg f = 2p+1, x=1/t^2: the leading power of dx/y at infinity is t^(2p−2). So that differential has a zero of order 2p−2 = deg K there (for p=3, the result should be ∝ t^4).

transcription_corrections: 'Setzt man v_p = u_p − α_p^p + v_p' is best read as forming ϑ(u_1 − α_1^{(p)} + v_1, …, u_p − α_p^{(p)} + v_p), i.e. e = α^{(p)} − v, with η_p arbitrary.
'(Σ_1^{p−1}α_1^{(ν)}, … Σ_1^{p−2}α_p^{(ν)})': the upper limit should be p−1.
'ϑ(Σ_1^{p−1}α_p^ν) = 0' denotes the full vector ϑ(Σ_1^{p−1}α_1^{(ν)}, …, Σ_1^{p−1}α_p^{(ν)}).
'außer den ∞ Werthenpaaren (ς_1, ζ_1)' most likely refers to the r fixed value pairs at the singular points of F, where all φ vanish (cf. 'der r Wurzeln' on the next page). It is not '∞'.
'wenn daher durch η_1, η_2 … η_{p−1}' should be read as 'wenn daher η_1 … η_{p−1} diese Punkte sind, ist (v) ≡ (−Σ_1^{p−1} α)'.
